title: Burst capacity headcount rebalancing and price sensitivities - Q4 2026
content:
Summary:

This working sheet explores a capacity-first headcount rebalance combined with 3 pricing-sensitivity scenarios to understand net unit economics when we deliberately tilt more workload to burst (on-demand) vs reserved capacity. Goal: identify low-friction headcount moves (Q4 hiring deferrals, temporary contractors, role reassignments) that reduce committed GPU spend while limiting customer latency regressions and revenue churn.

Key assumptions (high-level):
- Base rate: hosted API list price = $0.0035 per 1k tokens for gen (current public list) used as baseline for revenue sensitivity.
- Cost per token (current blended) = $0.0018 per 1k tokens when 60% reserved / 40% burst.
- Burst capacity cost multiplier = 2.1x of reserved per-token cost.
- We can delay 6 FTEs hiring (infra/serving) and hire 3 short-term contractors for Q4 to cover release windows.
- Elasticity: a 10% price increase on burst-eligible customers yields an estimated 2.5% immediate usage drop, and 6% over 6 months (customer-level heterogeneity).
- Target: keep gross margin > 60% at 65% reserved utilization.

Headcount plan (proposal, FTE) – high level table (quarters shown):

Roles 	 Q4-2026 	 Q1-2027 	 Q2-2027 	 Notes
Infra Eng (serving/runtime) 	 28 	 26 	 27 	 defer 4 hires in Q4, re-evaluate in Q1
SRE / Platform Ops 	 12 	 12 	 13 	 keep headcount for SLAs; 1 contractor Q4
Cost Ops / Capacity 	 6 	 7 	 7 	 +1 hire to monitor pricing tiers
Solutions Eng / Sales Eng 	 14 	 15 	 15 	 hire to support Dedicated deals
Finance (forecasting) 	 4 	 4 	 4 	 no change
Total FTE 	 64 	 64 	 66 	 net +2 by Q2 with rebalancing

Notes on HC moves: prioritize offering contractors to replace immediate infra hires (save ~30% fully loaded comp). Move two senior infra ICs part-time to cost-ops projects for 3 months to accelerate quantization ROI.

Capacity / spend model (simplified):
- Reserved commit (monthly) = $1.8M (current) covering 60% of peak token throughput.
- Burst spend (monthly) = $0.9M (current) covering 40% of peak.
- Scenario A (conservative): shift 10% of burst usage into lower-cost caching / model distillation -> burst spend down 8% -> monthly savings $72k.
- Scenario B (pricing tilt): increase burst price by 12% for non-committed customers -> expected burst usage down 6% -> net revenue change +4% (mixed effect) and cost down 6% -> improves margin by ~2.3ppt.
- Scenario C (aggressive re-commit): push customers to short reserved packages (30d micro-commits) with 6% discount vs list -> move 18% of burst to reserved -> requires +$350k/month commitment but reduces blended cost by ~14% -> breakeven on committed spend in ~9 months given retention assumptions.

Sensitivity matrix (illustrative):

Metric 	 Base 	 Scenario A 	 Scenario B 	 Scenario C
Monthly rev (hosted tokens) 	 $6.3M 	 $6.37M 	 $6.45M 	 $6.58M
Monthly cost 	 $3.24M 	 $3.168M 	 $3.048M 	 $2.792M
Gross margin 	 48.6% 	 50.2% 	 52.7% 	 57.6%
Net delta vs base 	 - 	 +1.6ppt 	 +4.1ppt 	 +9.0ppt

Scratch calculation examples (for transparency):
- If burst multiplier = 2.1x reserved; reserved per-token = $0.0014 per 1k; burst per-token = $0.00294 per 1k. Blended cost = 0.6*0.0014 + 0.4*0.00294 = $0.0018 per 1k.
- Scenario B price increase of 12% -> new effective burst price = 0.00294 * 1.12 = 0.00329; with elasticity -6% usage -> revenue change = + (price*usage) net; rough estimate +4% revenue on burst cohort.

Customer segmentation impact (qualitative):
- Enterprise customers: low elasticity; likely to absorb price shifts or convert to short-term reserved packages. Focus sales engineering to convert top 25 accounts.
- Developer/PLG users: higher elasticity; price increases will cause usage drop — mitigate with thresholded notifications and usage caps.
- Dedicated customers: unaffected by hosted pricing; potential upsell into dedicated/reserved.

Operational risks / mitigations:
- Risk: under-provisioned serving runtime leads to latency SLO misses when shifting workloads to burst; Mitigation: keep 10% buffer and use canary routing for traffic spikes.
- Risk: customer churn from pricing bump on low-touch tenants; Mitigation: grandfather existing customers for 45 days and A/B test price messaging.
- Risk: recruiting market slows rehire of deferred FTEs; Mitigation: convert open reqs to contractor budgets or postpone projects with lowest ROI.

Recommended actions (immediate, 30/60/90):
- 0–30d: approve deferral of 4 infra hires and authorize $140k contractor pool for Q4. Set up 2-week project to quantify quick wins from caching and model distillation.
- 30–60d: A/B test a 12% burst price increase on 10% random cohort with tracking on usage and churn triggers (stop if 30-day churn > 3% higher than control).
- 60–90d: Engage sales engineering to pilot 30d micro-commit bundles for top 50 accounts; track conversion and incremental committed ARR.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Get exact granularity of burst vs reserved by customer cohort (product datalake query: POR-usage-agg).
- Confirm contractor billing rate assumptions with People Ops (assume 1.6x FTE salary for fully loaded contractor).
- Run unit elasticity regressions on the last 18 months to update the -6% usage estimate (assign to Marco).
- Build a short financial dashboard to simulate sensitivity levels (linked PR in cost-models repo).

Appendix (quick scenario sensitivity sketch, for finance):
- Break-even table for additional committed spend in Scenario C: incremental commitment $350k/mo reduces blended cost by 14% -> monthly gross margin improvement = $453k -> payback ~0.77 months on incremental margin; conservative assumptions and retention reduce to 9 months. (double-check retention / churn assumptions before exec ask).

Notes: this is a working model (sheet + narrative). Numbers are intentionally rough — objective is to surface operational levers and low-friction headcount moves that can materially improve unit economics without heavy product changes.

Next steps: merge this into the master Q4 budgeting workbook (FIN: q4-2026-ops-capacity.xlsx) and schedule review with CFO + VP Infra on 2026-11-10.
